mainTopic: מעשר and wealth, stories of ריש לקיש's son, and whether sustenance comes for one person
overview: The amud opens with the דרשה that ״עשר תעשר״ means: give מעשר so that you become wealthy. In a story, רבי יוחנן teaches this to ריש לקיש's young son and tells him to go test it. When the boy objects that we may not test ה׳, רבי יוחנן answers from a פסוק in מלאכי that מעשר is the one exception. In a second story, the boy finds a hint in the תורה, from יוסף's brothers, for a פסוק in משלי, and his mother pulls him away from רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then brings רבי יוחנן's teaching that rain can come for one person, but sustenance comes only for the many. A ברייתא about the well, the clouds and the מן, given in the merit of מרים, אהרן and משה, seems to show sustenance coming for one person. The גמרא answers that משה asked for the many, so he counts like the many. The amud ends by starting a story about רבא's students and רב פפא.

steps.title: Give a tenth so you will become rich
steps.stepSummary: The doubled words ״עשר תעשר״ are read as a promise: give מעשר so that you will become wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A tithe shall you tithe" means: give a tithe so that you will become wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a דרשה on the doubled phrase ״עשר תעשר״: giving מעשר makes a person rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עשר (to give a tenth) sounds like עושר (wealth). The doubled phrase is read as cause and effect: tithe, and as a result you will grow rich.

keyTerms.meaning: "A tithe shall you tithe", the command to separate מעשר

steps.whyThisMatters: This promise is the base of the whole story that follows, including the idea that one may test ה׳ with מעשר.

phrases.english: "A tithe shall you tithe"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:22

phrases.english: Tithe so that you will become wealthy.
phrases.notes: It's a wordplay: עשר (a tenth) sounds like עושר (wealth).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening statement of this section

steps.title: The boy recites his פסוק and asks what it means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן meets the young son of ריש לקיש, asks him for the פסוק he learned, and the boy asks what ״עשר תעשר״ means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found the young son of ריש לקיש. He said: Tell me your verse. The boy said: "A tithe shall you tithe." The boy then asked: And what does "A tithe shall you tithe" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: A story starts. The boy recites the פסוק he learned and asks רבי יוחנן what it means, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a child for his פסוק was a common way to start a conversation. The boy's question about the doubled words opens the door for רבי יוחנן to teach the דרשה from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him, he met him
Tell me your verse (the one you learned today)

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְיָנוֹקָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan found the young son of Reish Lakish,
He said to him: Tell me your verse!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק the boy learned in school that day.

phrases.english: He said to him: "A tithe shall you tithe."
He said to him: And what does "A tithe shall you tithe" mean?
phrases.notes: Here the boy is the one asking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story built on the דרשה of step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the doubled phrase ״עשר תעשר״ mean?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains: tithe so you become rich
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers with the דרשה: give מעשר so that you will become wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give a tithe so that you will become wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the boy's question with the same דרשה we saw in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the meaning here. The story is now set up for the boy to ask for proof.

phrases.english: He said to him: Tithe so that you will become wealthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the boy's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase means tithe so that you will become wealthy.

steps.title: The boy asks: how do you know?
steps.stepSummary: The boy asks רבי יוחנן for the source of this promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The boy wants proof that giving מעשר really makes a person rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wordplay alone may not convince him. He asks מנא לך, the standard request for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the answer in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source or proof that tithing brings wealth?

steps.title: Go and test it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the boy to go and test the promise for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go and test it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of quoting a source, רבי יוחנן tells the boy to try it and see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof he offers is experience: give מעשר and watch the wealth come. This answer leads straight into the boy's objection in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go and test it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for proof
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Test it yourself and you will see.

steps.title: But we may not test ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The boy objects: the תורה says ״לא תנסו את ה׳״, so how can one test הקדוש ברוך הוא?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it allowed to test the Holy One, Blessed be He? But it is written: "You shall not test ה׳"!
steps.whatsHappening: The boy challenges רבי יוחנן's advice, using a פסוק that forbids testing ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לא תנסו את ה׳״ seems to forbid any test of ה׳. So telling someone to tithe in order to test whether he becomes rich looks forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: And is it permitted to test
the Holy One, Blessed be He?
But isn't it written: "You shall not test the Lord"!
phrases.notes: דברים 6:16

steps.triggerLanguage: ומי שרי לנסוייה להקדוש ברוך הוא והכתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the advice given in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's advice to go and test the promise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה forbids testing ה׳, so testing whether מעשר brings wealth should be forbidden.

steps.title: מעשר is the one exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי הושעיא: testing ה׳ is forbidden except with מעשר, because in מלאכי ה׳ Himself says ״ובחנוני נא בזאת״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי הושעיא said: Except for this case, as it says: "Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in My house, and test Me now with this, says ה׳ of hosts, if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you a blessing until there is more than enough."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge: the ban on testing ה׳ has one exception, מעשר, and he brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general ban stays in place. But in the פסוק in מלאכי, ה׳ Himself invites the test (״ובחנוני נא בזאת״) about bringing מעשר, so this one case is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source that one may test ה׳ through giving מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel ״לא תנסו את ה׳״. Testing ה׳ is still forbidden; מעשר is just the one exception.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Hoshaya said:
Except for this, as it is stated:
phrases.notes: He means: testing ה׳ is forbidden, except in this case of מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: ״הָבִיאוּ אֶת כׇּל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אֶל בֵּית הָאוֹצָר
phrases.english: "Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:10

phrases.english: that there may be food in My house,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחָנוּנִי נָא בָּזֹאת אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: and test Me now with this, says the Lord of hosts,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא אֶפְתַּח לָכֶם אֵת אֲרֻבּוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם
phrases.english: if I will not open for you the windows of heaven

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרִיקֹתִי לָכֶם בְּרָכָה עַד בְּלִי דָי״.
phrases.english: and pour out for you a blessing until there is more than enough."

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי אמר רבי הושעיא חוץ מזו שנאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception to a general rule, based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testing ה׳ is always forbidden, even with מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Testing ה׳ is forbidden, except with מעשר, where ה׳ Himself invites the test.

steps.title: What does ״עד בלי די״ mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words ״עד בלי די״ at the end of the פסוק mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "until there is more than enough" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to explain a phrase in the פסוק it just quoted, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״עד בלי די״ are unclear: how can a blessing go beyond 'enough'? The גמרא asks for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Until there is more than enough

phrases.english: What does "until there is more than enough" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a phrase from the פסוק quoted in step 7

steps.title: Your lips will wear out from saying 'enough'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא in the name of רב explains: the blessing will be so great that your lips will wear out from saying ״די״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב: Until your lips wear out from saying "enough."
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains ״עד בלי די״ with a wordplay: the blessing will be so huge that you will tire out from saying 'enough'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads בלי as related to יבלו (wear out) and די as the word 'enough'. So the blessing goes on long after you say 'enough'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said that Rav said:
Until your lips wear out
phrases.notes: יבלו (wear out) is a play on the word בלי in the פסוק.

phrases.english: from saying "enough."

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רמי בר חמא אמר רב עד שיבלו שפתותיכם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing will be so great that your lips will wear out from saying 'enough'.

steps.title: The boy: I could have learned it myself
steps.stepSummary: The boy tells רבי יוחנן that had he reached that פסוק, he would not have needed him or his teacher רבי הושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had reached that verse, I would not have needed you or your teacher הושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the boy's sharp remark that the answer is written openly in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy is saying the permission to test with מעשר is plain in מלאכי, so he would have found it on his own. It shows how sharp the young son of ריש לקיש was.

keyTerms.meaning: I would not have needed you

steps.whatToRemember: ״עשר תעשר״ means give מעשר and become wealthy. Testing ה׳ is forbidden, but מעשר is the one exception, since in מלאכי ה׳ says ״ובחנוני נא בזאת״, promising blessing ״עד בלי די״.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הֲוָת מָטֵי הָתָם
phrases.english: He said to him: If I had reached there,
phrases.notes: The boy is speaking: he hadn't yet learned up to that פסוק in מלאכי.

phrases.english: to this verse,
I would not have needed you
or Hoshaya your teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הוות מטי התם להאי פסוקא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the explanation of ״עד בלי די״
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The permission to test ה׳ through מעשר is stated openly in the פסוק in מלאכי.

steps.title: Another story: the boy recites a verse about foolishness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finds ריש לקיש's young son reciting a פסוק from משלי about a person who ruins his own way and then blames ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: On another occasion, רבי יוחנן found ריש לקיש's young son sitting and reciting: "A man's foolishness ruins his way, and his heart rages against ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second story about the same clever boy. This line sets the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְתוּ ("and furthermore") ties this story to the earlier one about מעשר. The פסוק describes someone who sins, gets into trouble, and then complains against ה׳ instead of looking at his own actions.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Yoḥanan found
the young son of Reish Lakish
who was sitting and saying:
"The foolishness of a man perverts his way,
phrases.notes: משלי 19:3

phrases.english: and his heart rages against the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְיָנוֹקֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second story about the same boy from the מעשר story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the פסוק from משלי that the story will discuss.

steps.title: Where is this verse hinted in the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wonders aloud: is there something in כתובים that has no hint in the תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן sat and wondered. He said: Is there anything written in כתובים that is not hinted at in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן cannot find where the idea of this פסוק appears in the תורה, so he asks out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question assumes a rule: every idea in כתובים should have a hint in the תורה. Since he cannot find one here, he is puzzled.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third part of תנ״ך

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan sat and wondered.
He said: Is there anything
that is written in the Writings
that is not hinted at in the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּכְתִיבִי בִּכְתוּבֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזִי בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the פסוק just quoted is hinted in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the תורה is the idea of "his heart rages against ה׳" hinted?

steps.title: The boy shows the hint from the brothers of יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The boy answers that the idea is in the תורה, in the words of יוסף's brothers: "What is this that God has done to us?"
steps.simpleTranslation: The boy said to him: Do you really think this is not hinted? Isn't it written: "Their heart sank, and they turned trembling to one another, saying: What is this that God has done to us?"
steps.whatsHappening: The boy answers רבי יוחנן's question by pointing to a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers had done wrong to יוסף, and now that trouble came they asked what God was doing to them. That matches the פסוק in משלי: a person's own actions bring trouble, and then he wonders why God did it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a word that pushes back on an assumption)

phrases.english: He said to him: Is that to say that this
is not hinted at?
But isn't it written:
"And their heart went out and they trembled,
phrases.notes: בראשית 42:28. These are יוסף's brothers speaking.

phrases.english: each man to his brother, saying:
What is this that God has done to us?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הָא מִי לָא רְמִיזִי וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question with a source from the תורה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hint is in בראשית 42:28, where יוסף's brothers, who had sinned, ask what God has done to them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן stares, and the mother takes the boy away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן looks hard at the boy, and his mother pulls him away so that he won't suffer what his father suffered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised his eyes and looked at him. His mother came and took him away. She said to him: Come away from him, so he does not do to you what he did to your father.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי יוחנן is impressed and stares at the boy, and the mother quickly removes her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother remembers that her husband ריש לקיש died after a painful clash with רבי יוחנן. She is afraid that רבי יוחנן's intense gaze could harm her son too.

keyTerms.meaning: From before him, away from him

steps.whatToRemember: The boy finds a hint in the תורה that even רבי יוחנן did not find, and the story ends with his mother protecting him.

phrases.english: He raised his eyes and looked at him.
His mother came and took him away.
She said to him: Come away from him,
so that he does not do to you
as he did to your father.
phrases.notes: She means ריש לקיש, who died after his clash with רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after the boy's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with the mother taking her son away from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Rain for one person, sustenance for the many
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that rain can come for the sake of one person, but sustenance comes only for the sake of the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Rain comes even for an individual. Sustenance comes for the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's teachings about rain and brings a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two blessings are compared. Rain can be given even because of one person who needs it. A blessing of sustenance comes only for a whole community.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think rain is not a kind of sustenance. The point is only that the rule differs: rain can come for one person, while the blessing of פרנסה comes for the many.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rain comes for the sake of an individual;
sustenance comes for the sake of many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מָטָר בִּשְׁבִיל יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, the גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's series of statements about rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain can fall for one person; sustenance comes only for the many.

steps.title: Proof that rain comes for one person
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "ה׳ will open for you His good treasure to give the rain of your land" speaks to one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rain comes for an individual, as it is written: "ה׳ will open for you His good treasure, to give the rain of your land."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves the first half of his teaching from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words לְךָ and אַרְצְךָ are singular, meaning "you" as one person. This shows that rain can be given for the sake of one person.

keyTerms.meaning: His good treasure, here the heavens

phrases.english: Rain comes for the sake of an individual, as it is written:
"The Lord will open for you His good treasure
phrases.notes: דברים 28:12. The proof is that לְךָ means "you" as one person.

phrases.english: to give the rain of your land."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.raayaObject: Rain can come for an individual.

steps.title: Proof that sustenance comes for the many
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "I will rain bread for you" speaks to the whole people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sustenance comes for the many, as it is written: "Behold, I will rain bread for you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves the second half of his teaching from a פסוק about the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word לָכֶם is plural, meaning "you all." Bread, which stands for sustenance, was given to the whole people together, so sustenance comes for the many.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן learns from singular and plural wording: rain is promised to "you" (one person), while bread is promised to "you all" (the many).

phrases.english: Sustenance comes for the sake of many, as it is written:
"Behold, I will cause bread to rain down for you."
phrases.notes: שמות 16:4. Here לָכֶם means "you all," so it speaks to the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement.

steps.title: Challenge: the מן came in the merit of משה alone
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the באר, ענן, and מן came in the merit of מרים, אהרן, and משה, so the מן came for one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that three good leaders arose for ישראל: משה, אהרן, and מרים. Three good gifts were given through them: the well, the cloud, and the מן. The well came in the merit of מרים, the pillar of cloud in the merit of אהרן, and the מן in the merit of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. It says the מן, which is food, came in the merit of just one person, משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that rain can come for one person, but sustenance only comes for the many (Step 15). The מן is pure sustenance, yet this ברייתא says it came because of משה alone. That looks like a direct contradiction. Step 29 spells out the problem, and step 30 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaders who provide for the people
The heavenly bread in the מדבר

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא goes on for a while about the well and the clouds, but the difficulty is only the line that the מן came in the merit of משה, one person, against Step 15. The גמרא states this outright at the end of the ברייתא (step 29).

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Three good leaders arose for Israel,
and they are: Moshe, Aharon, and Miriam.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת נִיתְּנוּ עַל יָדָם,
phrases.english: And three good gifts were given through them,
and they are: the well, the cloud, and the manna.
The well came in the merit of Miriam,
the pillar of cloud in the merit of Aharon,
the manna in the merit of Moshe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from Steps 15-17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that sustenance comes only for the many
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מן is sustenance, yet the ברייתא says it came in the merit of one individual, משה.

steps.title: When מרים died, the well disappeared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from the פסוקים that the באר left when מרים died, and then came back in the merit of משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When מרים died, the well disappeared, as it says: 'And מרים died there,' and right after it is written: 'And there was no water for the congregation.' The well came back in the merit of both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows that the well really depended on מרים. It proves this from two פסוקים next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים's death and the lack of water are placed one right after the other in the תורה. That closeness shows the water was tied to her merit. The well then returned because of משה and אהרן together.

phrases.english: When Miriam died, the well disappeared,
as it says: "And Miriam died there,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:1

phrases.english: and right after it is written: "And there was no water for the congregation,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:2

phrases.english: and it came back in the merit of the two of them.
phrases.notes: "The two of them" means משה and אהרן, who were still alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and proves the well was in מרים's merit
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 20:1-2, her death followed right away by no water

steps.title: When אהרן died, the clouds of glory disappeared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the ענני כבוד left when אהרן died and brings the פסוק about the כנעני king of ערד.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אהרן died, the clouds of glory disappeared, as it says: 'And the כנעני, the king of ערד, heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the second gift, the clouds, and links them to אהרן. It quotes a פסוק but has not yet explained how the פסוק proves it. That explanation comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the king 'heard' something but does not say what. The ברייתא will use that open question to show the clouds left.

keyTerms.meaning: Clouds of glory that protected ישראל

phrases.english: When Aharon died, the clouds of glory disappeared,
as it says: "And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, heard,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 33:40

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מרים's well to אהרן's clouds
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק about the king of ערד hearing

steps.title: What news did the king hear?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what report the king of ערד heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: What news did he hear?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about the פסוק to open up the proof. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק leaves out what the king heard. Asking this lets the ברייתא fill the gap with the clouds leaving.

phrases.english: What report did he hear?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the פסוק just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the king of ערד heard that made him attack

steps.title: He heard that אהרן died and the clouds left
steps.stepSummary: The king heard that אהרן died and the clouds left, and he thought he now had permission to attack ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He heard that אהרן had died and the clouds of glory had left, and he thought he had been given permission to fight against ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question: the news was that the clouds were gone. That is why the king felt free to attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clouds were ישראל's protection. Once they left with אהרן's death, an enemy thought ישראל was open to attack. This shows the clouds depended on אהרן.

phrases.english: He heard that Aharon had died
and the clouds of glory had disappeared,
and he thought he had been given permission
to wage war against Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He heard that אהרן died and the protecting clouds were gone

steps.title: The פסוק 'All the congregation saw that אהרן died'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא connects the clouds leaving to the פסוק that the congregation 'saw' that אהרן had died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And all the congregation saw that אהרן had died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings another פסוק to show the clouds left at אהרן's death. The next step explains how this פסוק should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק only says the people saw that אהרן died. The ברייתא says it hints to the clouds leaving. רבי אבהו will explain how that works.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And all the congregation saw that Aharon had died."
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק for the clouds leaving
steps.raayaObject: The clouds left when אהרן died

steps.title: רבי אבהו: read it as 'they were seen'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads וַיִּרְאוּ ('they saw') as וַיֵּרָאוּ ('they were seen'), meaning ישראל became exposed once the clouds left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Do not read 'they saw,' but 'they were seen.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains how the פסוק hints to the clouds. He reads the word as 'they were seen,' because without the clouds the people were now visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the vowels turns 'they saw' into 'they were seen.' Now the פסוק says ישראל became exposed when אהרן died. That only makes sense if the clouds that covered them had left.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Do not read "and they saw,"
but rather "and they were seen."
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels. The people were exposed because the clouds no longer hid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in Step 23 shows the clouds left
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק means ישראל 'were seen,' exposed without the clouds, when אהרן died

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the word כי has four meanings
steps.stepSummary: The reading fits ריש לקיש's teaching that כי can mean 'if,' 'perhaps,' 'but,' or 'because.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what ריש לקיש taught, for ריש לקיש said: The word כי is used in four ways: 'if,' 'perhaps,' 'but,' and 'because.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי אבהו's reading with ריש לקיש's rule about the word כי. Now the פסוק can read: 'They were seen, because אהרן died.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'they were seen,' the word כי can't mean 'that' anymore. ריש לקיש's rule lets כי mean 'because.' So the people were exposed because אהרן died and the clouds left.

keyTerms.meaning: As he taught from the פסוק

phrases.english: As Reish Lakish taught,
for Reish Lakish said:
The word "ki" is used in four senses:
if, perhaps, but, because.
phrases.notes: Here we use 'because': they were seen because אהרן died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's reading
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's reading of the פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's rule that כי can mean 'because'

steps.title: When משה died, all the gifts left
steps.stepSummary: The well and clouds came back for משה, and when משה died all three gifts left, as the פסוק says 'I cut off the three shepherds in one month.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Both came back in the merit of משה. When משה died, all of them disappeared, as it says: 'And I cut off the three shepherds in one month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא returns to its main story. After משה died, all three gifts were gone, and it brings a פסוק from זכריה as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's merit alone kept the well and clouds going after מרים and אהרן died. Once he died, nothing held them up. The פסוק about three shepherds in one month will be questioned next.

phrases.english: Both returned in the merit of Moshe,
phrases.notes: "Both" means the well and the clouds.

phrases.english: when Moshe died, all of them disappeared,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וָאַכְחִד אֶת שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָרֹעִים בְּיֶרַח אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: as it says: "And I cut off the three shepherds in one month,"
phrases.notes: זכריה 11:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side explanation to the main ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: All three gifts ended with משה's death

steps.title: They did not all die in one month
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how the three shepherds died in one month, since מרים died in ניסן, אהרן in אב, and משה in אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did they die in one month? מרים died in ניסן, אהרן in אב, and משה in אדר!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the simple reading of the פסוק. The three leaders died in three different months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'three shepherds' means משה, אהרן, and מרים, then 'one month' doesn't fit the facts. This forces a new way to read the פסוק.

phrases.english: But did they die in one month?
Didn't Miriam die in Nisan,
and Aharon in Av, and Moshe in Adar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of 'three shepherds in one month'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three leaders died in three different months

steps.title: The three gifts ended in one month
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that the three gifts given through them all stopped in one month, the month משה died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that the three good gifts given through them were cancelled, and all of them disappeared in one month.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: 'one month' is not about when they died. It is about when their gifts all ended together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts outlived מרים and אהרן because of משה. So all three ended together in משה's month. It was as if all three shepherds were cut off at once.
steps.whatToRemember: Each gift was tied to one צדיק: באר to מרים, ענן to אהרן, מן to משה. After מרים and אהרן died, משה's merit kept their gifts going, so all three ended when משה died. The ברייתא saying the מן came for משה alone is the challenge to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches
that the three good gifts were cancelled
that had been given through them,
and all of them disappeared in one month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means the three leaders died in one month
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means the three gifts given through them all ended in one month
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three gifts ended in the month משה died

steps.title: So sustenance can come for one person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא showed that the מן came in משה's merit, which seems to prove that פרנסה can come for an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that we find sustenance given for the sake of an individual!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem raised by the long ברייתא it just quoted. If the מן came because of משה, then sustenance can come for one person, which goes against the earlier teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching said rain can come for one person, but פרנסה only comes for the many. The ברייתא said the well, the clouds and the מן came in the merit of מרים, אהרן and משה, so the מן was sustenance given for one person. That clashes with the rule.

phrases.english: Apparently, we find sustenance for the sake of an individual!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging conclusion out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 18-28 and aims it at the earlier rule about פרנסה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that פרנסה is given only in the merit of the many
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the מן came in משה's merit. The מן is sustenance, so sustenance came for one person.

steps.title: משה counts like the many
steps.stepSummary: משה is different, because he asked for the many, so he is treated like the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה is different. Since he was asking on behalf of the many, he is considered like the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. משה was not asking for himself; he asked for all of ישראל, so his request counts as a request of the many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that sustenance only comes for the many stays in place. משה is a special case: someone who prays for the whole community is treated like the community itself. So the מן coming through משה does not break the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Sustenance comes only for the many. משה is not a real exception, because he prayed for the many and so counts like the many.

phrases.english: Moses is different,
since he requested it for the many,
he is like the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: משה's case is different because he asked for the community
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מן came for משה as one person, so sustenance can come for an individual.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה asked for the many, so he counts as the many. The rule that sustenance comes only for the many stands.

steps.title: רבא's students move to רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: Three students who used to learn before רבא came to רב פפא after רבא died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח, רב שמואל בר אידי and רב חייא from וסתניא used to be regulars before רבא. When רבא died, they came before רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It is setting the scene: three great students of רבא lost their teacher and moved to רב פפא's study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were top students who were used to רבא's level of teaching. That detail sets up the tension in the next step, when they come to a new teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him (in his presence, as students)
He passed away (literally, his soul rested)

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoaḥ
and Rav Shmuel bar Idi
and Rav Ḥiyya from Vastanya
were often found before Rava.
When Rava died,
they came before Rav Pappa.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ וְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִידִי וְרַב חִיָּיא מִוּוֹסְתַּנְיָא הֲווֹ שְׁכִיחִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story connected to the פסוק from זכריה about the three shepherds (step 26), after the discussion about פרנסה is resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבא's three students moved to רב פפא after רבא's death.

steps.title: The students signal to each other, and רב פפא is hurt
steps.stepSummary: Whenever רב פפא taught something that didn't make sense to them, the students signaled to each other, and רב פפא felt hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever רב פפא told them a teaching that did not seem right to them, they would signal to each other. He was hurt.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The students show quiet disrespect by signaling to one another, and רב פפא feels hurt by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students did not argue openly. They hinted to each other, as if to say רב פפא was not on רבא's level. The key point is that רב פפא was hurt, and that sets up what happens next in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: He felt hurt, was offended (literally, his mind grew weak)

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֵימַת דַּהֲוָה אָמַר לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
phrases.english: Whenever he would say a teaching to them
that did not seem reasonable to them,
they would gesture to each other.
He was offended.
phrases.notes: "He" is רב פפא; their signaling hurt his feelings.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אֵימַת דַּהֲוָה אָמַר לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא וְלָא הֲוָה מִסְתַּבְּרָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the students' signaling hurt רב פפא's feelings.
